strengths.I007: Fits selection directly to the benchmark's own outcome (wins against the baseline cards) with a residual model that collapses to today's BT ranking under few labels, and it absorbs length, hedge and family-match nuisance into covariates that are zeroed at selection, so verbosity and self-preference are explicitly removed rather than rewarded; testable offline by leave-one-brief-out AUC on existing runs.
strengths.I008: Zero extra token cost at equal budget, a principled Crowd-BT/Dawid-Skene vote model with explicit per-judge position (b_j) and self-preference (c_j) terms, and a Fisher-information schedule that spends votes on near-boundary top-6 pairs where the top-3 cut is actually decided.

verdicts.reason: I008 can only reweight judges and correct position and self-preference, so a bias shared by every LLM judge (verbosity, polish) passes through untouched, whereas I007 models those nuisance features directly and zeroes them at selection, so its gain is by construction not earned by longer or more polished cards.

strengths.I004: Improves the development stage by conditioning revision on an independent adversary's stated loss reasons, something a lone agent cannot generate for itself, with bias controls built into the mechanism (+/-5% token budget, both-order different-family verifier gate) and a no-reasons control arm that isolates the value of conditioning from mere re-editing.
strengths.I007: Requires no new generation and no run-cost increase, is testable offline on stored runs, and directly targets systematic selection error (Si et al. 2024) while defaulting to the current ranking when labels are scarce.

verdicts.reason: I004 makes the finalist cards themselves better, which carries to any brief a user submits, whereas I007 only reorders the existing finalists against labels defined by the benchmark comparison, so its ceiling is the quality of the pool and its gain risks being specific to the benchmark's rater panel (the Goodhart failure it names itself).
